subject: cultivars/TCUL-0001
notes: DJ Short's own 'Azure Haze' page states the cross (Silver Haze mother × famous Blueberry male) was made 'to create the same cross as the Blue Dream' — a first-party breeder statement confirming the Blueberry × Haze lineage. Corroborated by the DNA Genetics Blue Dream seed listing ('Genetics: Blueberry x Haze #1', https://dnagenetics.com/product/blue-dream-feminized/). No page for the name 'Blue Dream' itself exists on a first-party site; the Santa Cruz, California origin is a secondary-account claim. Previously recorded from the archive page (TCUL-0001).

subject: cultivars/TCUL-0009
wording: Released in 1990 by Sensi Seeds, Super Skunk backcrossed the classic Skunk #1 line with an exceptional Afghan hash plant
notes: First-party strain page confirms the release and the cross: 'Super Skunk has been winning awards and fans since its release in 1990… crossing our world-famous Skunk #1 with a robust, high yielding Afghan indica.' Previously recorded from the archive page (TCUL-0009). Breeder object is not a content entity.

subject: cultivars/TCUL-0009
notes: First-party strain page: 'Super Skunk is a cannabis variety that is a blend of Skunk #1 and a powerful Afghan indica.' The Afghan indica landrace parent has no archive page; only the Skunk #1 parent resolves to a content entity.

subject: cultivars/TCUL-0007
wording: Bred in California during the 1970s by Sacred Seeds (David Watson / Sam the Skunkman) and refined in the Netherlands by Sensi Seeds
notes: Sensi Seeds' Skunk #1 page confirms Sensi's role ('the world's first stable indica-sativa hybrid') and the skunk lineage; Sensi's own blog 'Sam the Skunkman: The Evolution of Hybrids' (https://sensiseeds.com/en/blog/sam-the-skunkman-the-evolution-of-hybrids/) attributes the original Skunk #1 to Sam the Skunkman's time with Sacred Seeds. Sacred Seeds has no official site; this is the closest first-party attestation available.

subject: cultivars/TCUL-0004
wording: Developed in the Netherlands during the mid-1990s and named in honor of cannabis activist Jack Herer
notes: First-party strain page: 'This flagship of the Sensi Seeds barn is named after the cannabis activist Jack Herer.' Sensi's own grow-report blog (https://sensiseeds.com/en/blog/jack-herer-feminized-grow-report/) confirms the Haze × Northern Lights #5 × Shiva Skunk combination.

subject: cultivars/TCUL-0006
wording: Brought to the Netherlands in the 1980s, Sensi Seeds stabilized several phenotypes (most notably Northern Lights #5)
notes: First-party strain page: 'thought to have originated in the States, before being taken to The Netherlands. There, Sensi Seeds developed it into the variety that it is today, enhancing its Afghani and Thai genetics.'

subject: cultivars/TCUL-0002
wording: Originating in the late 1970s through breeder DJ Short and introduced to European seed banks by Dutch Passion in the 1990s
notes: Dutch Passion's Blueberry page presents the '1970's Original Blueberry' and states the varieties were 'originally bred by DJ Short and adopted by Dutch Passion in a cooperation with the Canadian breeder.' Page is JS-rendered; the claim text was verified from the official page's indexed content on 2026-08-09. Cross-corroboration: DNA Genetics' Blue Dream page describes Blueberry as a cross of Afghani, Purple Thai, and Thai — consistent with this archive page's lineage.

subject: cultivars/TCUL-0003
wording: Imported from South Africa in the 1970s and acclimated to European outdoor and indoor cultivation by Dutch Passion
notes: Official page describes 'a pure landrace Sativa dominant variety which originates from South Africa.' The 'imported in the 1970s' detail in the wording is archive-sourced and not explicitly restated on the page; Dutch Passion's own blog describes Durban Poison as a photoperiod original from the 1980s. Origin claim notes the line is an originally imported landrace selection, not a Dutch Passion invention.

subject: cultivars/TCUL-0005
wording: Renamed from 'Mazar-i-Sharif' in 1997, Dutch Passion improved this classic Afghan resin producer by crossing the northern Afghan landrace with Skunk #1
notes: Official page: 'Mazar is an original Afghan Indica crossed with a special phenotype from our legendary Skunk #1.' The 'renamed from Mazar-i-Sharif in 1997' detail in the wording is archive-sourced and not explicitly restated on the page.

subject: cultivars/TCUL-0005
wording: Afghan Indica Landrace (Mazar-i-Sharif, Northern Afghanistan) × Skunk #1
notes: Official page explicitly confirms the Skunk #1 cross ('an original Afghan Indica crossed with a special phenotype from our legendary Skunk #1'). The Afghan landrace parent has no archive page; only the Skunk #1 parent resolves to a content entity.

subject: cultivars/TCUL-0008
wording: Popularized in North America and introduced to global seed catalogs by Dutch Passion
notes: Dutch Passion lists Strawberry Cough, confirming the seed-bank offering. The breeder attribution to Kyle Kushman is widely reported in strain databases (CannaConnection: https://www.cannaconnection.com/strains/strawberry-cough; Medical Jane review crediting 'the breeder': https://www.medicaljane.com/review/kyle-kushmans-strawberry-cough-from-buds-roses/) but is contested: see CLM-0014 (Jeff Cavanagh) and the source_disagrees_with record CLM-0015. Kushman's own public position is that he received the cut as a gift and popularized it rather than bred it, which complicates the 'breeder' framing itself. Per the source-role model, a seed-bank/catalog page is not strong evidence for breeder attribution; the claim stays 'claimed'.

subject: cultivars/TCUL-0008
wording: Strawberry Cough 'was not made by Kyle Kushman. The real breeder? A man named Jeff Cavanagh'

source.name: Overgrow forum — 'The Real Story Behind Strawberry Cough'

notes: Community forum claim (May 2025) that Jeff Cavanagh bred the original Strawberry Cough and that Kyle Kushman popularized or rebranded it. Per the source-role model, forum sources are weak identity authority; even within the thread, commenters note Kushman's own account is that he received the cut as a gift. No first-party source from Cavanagh is attached. Conflicts with CLM-0013; see CLM-0015.

subject: CLM-0013
wording: Who bred the original Strawberry Cough: Kyle Kushman / Dutch Passion (CLM-0013) vs Jeff Cavanagh (CLM-0014)
notes: Documents the attribution dispute for cultivars/TCUL-0008. Both sides are retained at status 'claimed'; neither is promoted. The dispute is partly semantic: the widespread attribution treats Kushman as breeder/popularizer, while the Cavanagh claim distinguishes breeder from popularizer. For source_disagrees_with, subject/object reference the two conflicting claim IDs.
